evals.prompt: Explicitly review two sessions where the canonical check returned success after a forbidden import. Propose improvements only. An existing dedicated check rejects both historical mistakes but is not invoked by the canonical command.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the wiring gap and existing owner, retains scope, and proposes replay of the historical cases plus legitimate controls.
expectations: Repairs existing control before duplicating it
Cites both occurrences
Proposes rather than implements
Defines rejection and legitimate-case evidence

evals.prompt: Review and implement the authorized guard repair. A connected substring check rejects legal comments as well as forbidden imports. Both past illegal imports and valid comment-only files are available.
evals.expected_output: Repairs the guard without weakening the forbidden-import contract, proves historical rejection and legitimate acceptance, and retains independent review evidence.
expectations: Preserves the behavior contract
Executes the canonical path
Historical cases fail for the intended reason
Legitimate cases pass
Runs three independent lenses and synthesis or reports coverage gaps

evals.prompt: Review a session that read a clear check-before-commit rule, ignored an actual nonzero check, and called the task verified. The user also requested English for this one PR.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes execution failure from missing instructions and scopes the one-off choice to that task.
expectations: Does not duplicate clear guidance
Checks the actual failure and command owner
Does not turn a one-off choice into a global preference
Keeps product code and trackers outside review-only authorization

evals.prompt: Review a clean session with working canonical checks, wired CI, verified output and no recurring friction.
evals.expected_output: Allows no retained improvements rather than inventing rules or tools.
expectations: Empty result is valid
Does not count suggestion volume as quality
Keeps review-only scope

evals.prompt: Review an identified session whose primary history is unavailable. A digest and a current diff are accessible, but the working tree includes another agent's changes.
evals.expected_output: Reports the history gap, uses the digest with explicit limits and does not attribute all current changes to the session.
expectations: Verifies session and project scope
Labels digest evidence
Separates current state from historical attribution
Avoids unrelated session mining

evals.prompt: Use the authorized review results to implement one repeated mistake class. A legacy import remains possible; several historical violations exist. The user requested one commit per class and cannot provide CI access.
evals.expected_output: Examines architecture, types and deterministic enforcement in order, uses a ratchet if appropriate, records the enforcement owner and reports CI as pending.
expectations: Retains architecture-first priority
Explains why higher levels do not fit
Keeps implementation and proof in the class commit
Maintains the scoped enforcement table
Does not claim unavailable CI ran

evals.prompt: The user is midway through a feature task and corrects a typo. No retrospective skill was explicitly requested.
evals.expected_output: The runtime keeps this user-only skill out of implicit invocation; ordinary work continues.
expectations: SKILL.md disables model invocation
OpenAI policy disables implicit invocation
Does not use a typo as permission for environment audit

evals.prompt: Implement a previously selected and authorized correction to a stale command in an existing skill. The incident, owner, proposed edit and unchanged current target can all be verified. No new cause or broader repair is involved.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the verified conclusion, loads Instructions for the edit, and validates the affected command without restarting the retrospective.
expectations: Verifies prior evidence, current target and authorization
Does not restart three-lens retrospective to implement an unchanged conclusion
Loads only the applicable repair reference
Executes the corrected command and preserves unrelated guidance

evals.prompt: Implement an authorized guard precision repair. The only recorded incidents are two legal comment-only inputs that the canonical guard rejected. The contract bans actual legacy_api imports, not mentions in comments. No historical forbidden-import incident is available.
evals.expected_output: Makes historical legal inputs pass, checks forbidden imports using clearly labelled new control cases, and preserves the original canonical path and scope.
expectations: Historical false-positive inputs become accepted
Does not invent a historical forbidden-import incident
New violation controls remain rejected
Reports actual proof through the canonical command

evals.prompt: Implement two selected authorized findings: the canonical check drops explicit target arguments, and the same target contract is buried in an existing skill. Current source and incident evidence confirm both findings.
evals.expected_output: Routes the execution repair to Guardrails and the placement repair to Instructions, retaining both causes and their separate verification.
expectations: Routes each finding rather than classifying the whole task once
Allows both repair references for a mixed cause
Keeps structural repair type separate from Accepted or Backlog status
Scopes any executors to their own findings and rules

evals.prompt: Implement a previously approved wiring repair. Inspection now shows the dedicated guard was removed and the canonical command has changed; the previous incident receipts refer to the old entry point. Another selected instruction edit is unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Reopens the changed finding for evidence and independent review, preserves the unaffected conclusion, and does not implement the obsolete wiring proposal.
expectations: Verifies current target before reusing conclusions
Revisits the changed cause or remedy
Preserves unaffected findings
Does not apply stale authorization to a materially different repair

evals.prompt: Review a single incident where a documented guard failed to inspect an explicitly requested target. Propose improvements only; no writes, commits or tracker publication are authorized.
evals.expected_output: Runs the new-retrospective review, retains a supported structural proposal without inventing recurrence, and specifies its proof as pending.
expectations: Retains three independent lenses and separate synthesis for new review
A single incident may justify a structural finding
Does not call one incident a repeated class
Proposes verification without implementing or reconciling unchanged guidance
